# Cross-Condition Network Module Comparison

Comparing biological co-occurrence networks between healthy and diseased states requires evaluating whether functional modules share feature composition. `cliomicplot` calculates hypergeometric overlap and Representation Factors ($RF$) through `type_module_compare()`.

## Mathematical Formulation of Module Overlap

Given a background universe of $N$ total features, module $M_1$ from Condition 1 containing $|M_1|$ features, and module $M_2$ from Condition 2 containing $|M_2|$ features, the overlap count is $k = |M_1 \cap M_2|$.

### Jaccard Similarity Index

The Jaccard index measures the proportion of shared features relative to the union:

$$J(M_1, M_2) = \frac{|M_1 \cap M_2|}{|M_1 \cup M_2|} = \frac{k}{|M_1| + |M_2| - k}$$

### Representation Factor ($RF$)

The Representation Factor quantifies whether the observed overlap exceeds what is expected by chance ($RF > 1.0$ indicates enrichment, $RF < 1.0$ indicates depletion):

$$RF = \frac{|M_1 \cap M_2|}{\mathbb{E}[|M_1 \cap M_2|]} = \frac{k}{\frac{|M_1| \cdot |M_2|}{N}} = \frac{k \cdot N}{|M_1| \cdot |M_2|}$$

### Hypergeometric Overlap Significance

The probability of observing $k$ or more shared features by random chance is calculated from the hypergeometric distribution:

$$P(X \ge k) = \sum_{x=k}^{\min(|M_1|, |M_2|)} \frac{\binom{|M_2|}{x} \binom{N - |M_2|}{|M_1| - x}}{\binom{N}{|M_1|}}$$

## Visualizing Module Overlap with `type_module_compare`

`cliplot()` accepts either node-level cluster assignments or precomputed overlap matrices:

```{r module-compare-demo, fig.width=7.5, fig.height=5.2}
library(cliomicplot)

# Reproducible node-level community assignments across discovery and replication networks
set.seed(42)
n_features <- 90
features <- paste0("Taxon_", 1:n_features)
net1_mods <- sample(c("M1_Barrier", "M2_Inflammation", "M3_Sebum"), n_features, replace = TRUE)
net2_mods <- net1_mods
# Rewire 30% of features in replication network
rewired_idx <- sample(1:n_features, 27)
net2_mods[rewired_idx] <- sample(c("ModA_Th2", "ModB_Stratum", "ModC_Lipid"), 27, replace = TRUE)

df_nodes <- data.frame(
  Feature     = features,
  Discovery   = net1_mods,
  Replication = net2_mods
)

p_comp <- cliplot(
  Replication ~ Discovery,
  data   = df_nodes,
  type   = type_module_compare(
    fill_by        = "rf",            # Fill by Representation Factor
    show_stars     = TRUE,            # Display significance asterisks
    show_totals    = TRUE,            # Display marginal totals
    total_universe = 120              # Universe size N
  ),
  preset = "nature",
  title  = "Cross-Network Module Preservation: Discovery vs Replication"
)
p_comp
```

Significant overlaps ($P < 0.001$, $***$) identify conserved biological functional units that persist despite phenotypic transitions.
